units.blurb: Baker's percentages, lean, enriched and laminated doughs, and pastry doughs.

topics.title: Baker's Percentages
topics.short: Every ingredient is written as a percent of the flour's weight: flour is 100%, water 65% means 650 g of water for 1,000 g of flour.
topics.trouble: Learners make the percents add up to 100; in baker's math the flour alone is 100%.

topics.title: Lean Doughs: Flour, Water, Salt and Yeast
topics.short: Mix, knead to build gluten, ferment, shape, proof and bake. Hydration (water as a percent of flour) sets the texture; salt is about 2%.
topics.trouble: Bakers add salt straight onto the yeast, or judge proofing by the clock instead of the dough.

topics.title: Enriched and Laminated Doughs
topics.short: Butter, eggs, milk and sugar make soft, rich doughs (brioche, challah); folding a sheet of butter into dough again and again makes layers (croissant, puff pastry).
topics.trouble: Bakers let the butter get warm while laminating, so it melts into the dough and the layers disappear.

topics.title: Pie Dough, Pâte Sucrée and Pâte à Choux
topics.short: 3-2-1 pie dough (flour, fat, water by weight), sweet tart dough made by creaming, and choux paste cooked on the stove, then beaten with eggs so it puffs in the oven.
topics.trouble: Bakers overwork pie dough, which toughens it, or open the oven while choux puffs and it collapses.

topics.title: Custards: Crème Anglaise and Pastry Cream
topics.short: Crème anglaise is milk, yolks and sugar stirred over gentle heat until it coats a spoon (about 170°F to 180°F); pastry cream adds starch and must come to a boil to thicken.
topics.trouble: Cooks boil crème anglaise and curdle it, or stop pastry cream before it boils, so it thins later.

topics.title: Chocolate and Tempering
topics.short: Tempering melts, cools and gently rewarms chocolate so the cocoa butter sets in its stable form: shiny, snapping, not streaky.
topics.trouble: Cooks let a drop of water get into melting chocolate, which makes it seize into a stiff paste.

topics.title: Sugar Stages and Caramel
topics.short: As syrup cooks, water boils off and the temperature rises: thread, soft ball, firm ball, hard ball, soft crack, hard crack, then caramel.
topics.trouble: Cooks stir a sugar syrup that is crystallizing, or leave the pan to answer the phone; caramel goes from perfect to burnt in seconds.

topics.title: Plated Desserts
topics.short: A main item, a sauce, something crisp, something cold, and a garnish that belongs: contrast in texture, temperature and color.
topics.trouble: Cooks pile on garnish that adds nothing to the taste, such as a mint sprig on everything.
